subsystems.name: X-ray collector
subsystems.role: gathers enough X-ray photons from a faint pulsar to build a usable pulse profile.
parts: nested grazing-incidence mirror shells or coded-mask aperture

subsystems.name: Photon-counting detector
subsystems.role: detects individual X-ray photons and stamps each one with an arrival time.
parts: silicon drift detectors or microchannel plates

subsystems.name: Time base
subsystems.role: the reference oscillator against which photon arrival times are measured.
parts: ultra-stable oscillator or miniature atomic clock

subsystems.name: Pulsar catalogue and barycentre model
subsystems.role: supplies the pulse 'beacons' and converts onboard times into a common reference frame.

subsystems.name: Navigation solver
subsystems.role: turns time-of-arrival residuals into position and clock corrections.

subsystems.name: Attitude and pointing
subsystems.role: aims the detector at each pulsar in turn, since only one line of sight can be observed at a time.

buildSteps.title: Choose the beacons
buildSteps.detail: Millisecond pulsars are picked for sharp pulses and decades-long rotational stability; long radio timing campaigns establish their spin, proper motion and binary parameters.

buildSteps.title: Build the X-ray catalogue
buildSteps.detail: Because X-ray and radio pulse shapes differ, the profile of each chosen pulsar must be measured in X-rays by an observatory-class telescope and stored as a template.

buildSteps.title: Size the detector
buildSteps.detail: A photon budget calculation sets the collecting area and observing time needed for a target accuracy, since signal-to-noise improves roughly with the square root of observing time.

buildSteps.title: Build and qualify the payload
buildSteps.detail: Detectors, concentrators and electronics are assembled to microsecond time resolution and put through vibration, thermal-vacuum and radiation testing.

buildSteps.title: Provide the clock
buildSteps.detail: An ultra-stable oscillator is characterised so that its drift over hours is small enough for the pulsars themselves to correct over days.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate on the ground
buildSteps.detail: A pulsed X-ray source simulates pulsar arrival times, verifying the whole chain from photon detection to time tag against a known input.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate against known truth
buildSteps.detail: In orbit, the instrument observes selected pulsars while the spacecraft's true position is known from GNSS or ground tracking, so measured arrival times can be compared with predicted ones.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: The onboard filter is then fed only pulsar data and its autonomous position and clock solution is compared with the truth solution — the step that turns an instrument into a navigator.

prerequisites.why: radio observatories have timed these pulsars for decades; their long-term rotational regularity rivals atomic clocks.

prerequisites.tech: Space-qualified X-ray optics and photon-counting detectors
prerequisites.why: observatory-class X-ray telescopes fly today, but compact, low-mass navigator payloads are only now being demonstrated.
deep-space atomic clocks have flown, yet low-mass oscillators stable enough over multi-day arcs are still improving.
onboard arrival times must be referred to a common barycentric frame before they can be differenced against stored models.
the solver, scheduler and fault handling must run on a spacecraft processor with no ground support.

pathway.milestone: in-orbit demonstrations: an X-ray timing payload on the ISS achieved onboard position fixes from a few pulsars, and a dedicated Chinese test satellite flew in 2016
pathway.unlocks: proof that the measurement chain works in space.

pathway.milestone: purpose-built smallsat navigators with lighter concentrators and better clocks
pathway.unlocks: regular kilometre-class fixes at mass and power a normal mission can carry.

pathway.milestone: operational use as an adjunct on deep-space missions
pathway.unlocks: less reliance on ground-station tracking for routine orbit determination and a fallback when tracking is unavailable.

pathway.milestone: hybrid navigation fusing pulsar timing with optical sightings of planets and asteroids plus inter-spacecraft links
pathway.unlocks: faster convergence and better accuracy than any one method alone.

pathway.milestone: a maintained multi-pulsar catalogue and timing grid shared across spacecraft
pathway.unlocks: absolute position and a common time standard anywhere in the galaxy, including for interstellar precursor missions.
